title: Quick quiz: how windows and doors work
intro: Ten questions on the technology. Tap an answer to see why.
messages: Worth another read of the guide above.

qs.q: What does a window's U-factor tell you?
options: How fast heat escapes through it
qs.why: A lower U-factor means better insulation.

qs.q: What does SHGC stand for on a window label?
options: Solar heat gain coefficient, or how much sun heat comes through
qs.why: A low number cuts summer heat. A higher number helps winter warmth on sunny sides.

qs.q: Why do double and triple panes help?
options: Gas-filled gaps between panes slow heat flow
qs.why: The sealed space between panes acts as insulation.

qs.q: What does a low-E coating do?
options: Reflects heat while letting light through
qs.why: It is a very thin coating on the glass.
Vinyl, fibreglass, wood and aluminum each handle heat and weather differently.

qs.q: Why does installation matter so much?
options: Gaps around the frame leak air even with great glass
Windows only work if they are painted
qs.why: Good flashing, shims and air sealing around the frame are part of the job.

qs.q: What is a low-cost first step against drafts?
qs.why: Sealing leaks often costs far less than new windows and gives a quick payback.

qs.q: On an air leakage rating, which is better?
qs.why: It measures how much air passes through the closed window.

qs.q: How do you pick ENERGY STAR windows?
options: Choose the rating for your climate zone
qs.why: Ratings differ by region because a cold place needs different glass than a hot one.

qs.q: Which door usually loses less heat?
options: An insulated fibreglass or steel door with a foam core
A door that is mostly glass
qs.why: Foam-core doors resist heat flow far better than hollow or glass-heavy ones.
